exact_statement: For each d>=2, let P be the squared Fourier law of the fair Boolean AND sign 2 product_i X_i-1. For every Fourier-set event E containing the empty set and r nonempty sets with 1<=r<=2^d-2, the full normalized conditional law Q=P(.|E) is not the normalized product Fourier law of any Boolean gate on any finite cube with rational product biases, for any Fourier phases and with the empty label preserved. Writing a=2^(d-1), Q(empty)=(a-1)^2/((a-1)^2+r) has irrational square root because its denominator lies strictly between consecutive integer squares. This is an admission obstruction, not an FEI disproof; Q remains an allowed normalized reference. The rational-bias restriction is essential, as the AND2 event retaining empty and one singleton is realized by a sign input at bias(1+1/sqrt2)/2.
